payload.name: Preserve non-contradicted facts when updating memories
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with new evidence about the same event or state, keep all previously stored facts that are not contradicted.
content: Before applying UPDATE or MERGE to an existing memory, compare the incoming evidence against the current content and identify which existing facts remain valid.
Preserve every existing fact that is not explicitly contradicted by the new message; combine it with the new details in the resulting content instead of replacing the full memory.
Treat messages that add context to an already recorded event (location, timing, feelings, outcomes) as enrichments: the updated memory must contain both the original facts and the new facts.
Remove only the specific portion that is superseded or corrected by new evidence; never let a new paraphrase delete other true facts from the same memory.

solves: A later message about an already-stored event caused an UPDATE to overwrite the entire memory content and silently drop a previously recorded, still-true fact. This happens when construction rewrites a memory from the new evidence instead of merging non-conflicting facts. Future sessions with recurring topics such as activities, trips, or relationships can hit the same loss; the rule generalizes to any UPDATE/MERGE where new details elaborate but do not contradict existing memory.
